explanation: This edge makes the two chains one picture. It records a transfer of a technique, a people and a supply chain. The cane that transformed Barbados came from Dutch Brazil in 1640. Colonel James Drax went to Pernambuco that year and bought a triple-roller mill and a set of copper cauldrons. The Sephardic families who had left Iberia for Dutch Brazil, in the cited account, did much for the early success of the Barbadian industry. Dutch traders supplied the equipment, the financing, the enslaved Africans and the shipping to Europe. The West India Company lost what it had built at Recife by 1654, and by then it had already been carried north.
